Hi Alicia — thanks for the heads up. Short answers up front:

- We can accept a partial prepayment on the first invoice (typically 30% retainer) on a one-time basis for new customers.
- We also support PO-locking semantics in most customer portals: invoices with a matching PO number and the vendor ID will remain in "pending PO" until the PO is released by Helios AP. That is our preferred model where the portal supports it.

I've attached our Redwood_AP_Packet_v2.pdf and Bank_Mandate_Form.pdf with the fields Helios usually needs (W-9, remit-to, tax ID, ACH routing, and our invoice header sample). For tax evidence: we are a US entity (EIN on the W-9 in packet). If Helios needs additional forms (e.g., state tax exemption), let me know.

Required next steps from your side (to get the PO locking flow active):
1) Provide the Helios vendor_id that the portal assigns (or a portal invite so we can confirm vendor profile fields).
2) Ensure the PO number appears in the "PO number" field when you create invoices in the portal — our gateway matches on that field exactly.
3) For retainer/prepayment: confirm a wire or ACH will be used and whether the payment will be held to offset the first invoice (we can apply as credit).

If you prefer the prepayment route I can have billing issue a pro-forma invoice for 30% (or 50% if you prefer). If you're doing PO-locking, we'll need a signed order form + the vendor_id to validate.

I've CC'd AP as well so they have the packet. Attaching: Redwood_AP_Packet_v2.pdf (AP checklist, remittance header, W-9) and Bank_Mandate_Form.pdf (ACH/wire fields).

Let me know what you prefer and I can follow up with an invoice or next steps.

Best,

Hi team — quick notes from infra/billing side:

- PO-locking: our billing gateway supports two matching modes for portals: (A) Strict PO match: invoice is accepted only if "PO Number" equals the PO in the portal; (B) Vendor ID + PO match: portal provides a vendor_id and the invoice must include both vendor_id and PO. Mode B is more robust (prevents accidental matches) but requires Helios to provide vendor_id.
- If Helios wants the gateway to hold payment until PO release, we can set invoices to status=holding until AP moves the PO to "Approved". That is purely a portal-side workflow; we only need a vendor mapping (portal vendor_id -> our vendor_uid) and the PO format.
- For prepayments: we can accept ACH/wire. If they send a retainer, billing will post as credit against the next invoice. ACH is preferred (lower fees).
- Tax/VAT: Redwood is US-based. W-9 included in packet. If Helios is processing through a foreign entity or needs W-8 instead, they'll need to flag that now. No VAT on US-to-US services.
- Documents we need to complete their vendor profile: Completed Vendor_Enrollment_Form (we can accept via portal upload), W-9 (in the packet), company registration (redwood EIN if requested), remit-to bank mandate.

I'll prepare a short vendor mapping doc for Helios (include expected field names for vendor_id, remit_to, invoice_header) and upload to the shared doc link. Marissa — can you coordinate the commercial ask about retainer amount (30% vs 50%) with the customer? If they want 50% we should route to CRO for approval.

Karthik
Principal Billing Engineer | Redwood Inference
